To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, perceived risk, and trust are all important factors for consumer acceptance of e-commerce.

(1) perceived usefulness is the key driver of consumer acceptance of e-commerce; (2) perceived ease of use and perceived risk are the next most important drivers of consumer acceptance of electronic commerce; (3) trust in the e-commerce site is a key driver of consumer perceived ease of use, perceived risk, and intention to transact; and (4) perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use of perceived risk are key drivers of on-line transaction behavior.
